Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. To make the initial SI onboarding smooth and predictable, I want to align on two things before our kickoff next week: capacity assumptions (how many concurrent users/customers and expected traffic profile) and the onboarding governance (who signs off on milestones and where the MA lives).

Proposed immediate asks:
- Can you confirm pilot cohort size (number of customers and expected daily active users) and a rough token estimate?
- Are there any procurement/legal constraints we should expect for the MA / SOW?
- Please find attached: SI_Enablement_Checklist_v1.xlsx (draft) — we use this to stage enablement tasks.

Suggested kickoff agenda (30–45m):
1) Introductions + scope
2) Pilot capacity targets and KPIs
3) Security/compliance Qs + next steps for questionnaire
4) Timeline & mutual action plan signoff

If that looks good I’ll circulate a short agenda and Marcus will provide a capacity estimate. Can you confirm availability for Nov 24–25 for a 30m sync?

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-17T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Solution Integrator: Capacity & Onboarding Governance — capacity estimate

Team —

Quick numbers based on the 3-customer pilot + burst headroom:
- Baseline: 250k tokens/day -> ~0.9 GPU-hours/day on our small inference pool (NVIDIA T4 equivalent) assuming batching.
- Burst (450k tokens/day): ~1.6 GPU-hours/day; recommend we plan for 3–4 GPU-hours/day to include peak concurrency and safe headroom.
- Recommendation: start with shared pool + autoscale rules, but have a dedicated reserved pool (2 GPUs) ready if latency SLOs are tight during pilot ramp.

I attached a quick workbook (capacity_model_Q4.xlsx) with assumptions and simple cost breakouts. If we go dedicated we should propose a short reserved commit for the pilot period to keep latency predictable.

Marcus
Senior Infra PM — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_model_Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)
